problem.text: If $f(x + y) = f(xy)$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, and $f(2019) = 17$, what is the value of $f(17)$?

steps.title: Where to start: plug in $x = 0$
steps.body: The equation holds for all real $x$ and $y$, so we may choose any values we like. A good first try in a functional equation is $0$. Here it is especially useful, because $0$ makes the product $xy$ collapse to a single number while the sum $x + y$ stays free.

your_turn.prompt: If $x = 0$, what do $x + y$ and $xy$ become?

steps.title: The function is constant
steps.body: So the equation becomes $f(y) = f(0)$ for every real $y$. Whatever input we use, the output is the same number $f(0)$: the function is constant.

your_turn.prompt: Check that any constant function $f(x) = k$ really satisfies $f(x + y) = f(xy)$.
your_turn.answer: Both sides equal $k$, so the equation holds.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Since every output equals $f(0)$, we have $f(0) = f(2019) = 17$, and then $f(17) = f(0) = 17$. The answer is **$17$**.
